market_context.summary: The Fed HIKED. The FOMC raised the target range 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 (effective 2026-09-17), projects PCE inflation at 3.7% and core PCE at 3.4% for 2026, and its own median dot puts fed funds at 4.1% by end-2026 — another hike — held at 4.1% through 2027 with no cut until 2028. Chair Warsh: "Inflation is too high and has been for too long." This is a tightening cycle against elevated inflation, and the research phase initially read it backwards from the tape and corrected itself against the primary sources at 06:31 ET. Policy is now 3.75-4.00% against a 5.01% 10-year and a 4.74% 2-year, a +0.27 10y-2y curve steepened by the long end pricing term premium. The day's real signal is dispersion, not direction: a 5% 10-year is precisely what breaks housing, RVs, building products and the financed consumer while doing nothing to the AI capex cycle. LCII sits 37.4% off its high, THO 19.0%, FERG 20.3%, COST 18.5%, NKE 31.5%, KBH 23.7% and BCC 14.6% — all rate-sensitive consumer durables — while SMH rose 2.76%, QQQ 1.73%, and DINO and XLE closed at their 120-day highs. The 2026-09-17 session was broadly risk-on with bonds rallying alongside stocks, which is the signature of a fully-priced hike rather than a dovish one.

data_quality_notes:
RESEARCH RAN TO COMPLETION. notes.md carries a RESEARCH COMPLETE block at 06:33 ET, so `truncated` is false and nothing here is reconstructed from fragments. 13 unique candidates across 21 captured lines; the last entry per symbol was taken, since EEM, GLD, TLT, PFE and NKE were each re-captured after a mid-run correction.

THE ONE THING NOT TO LOSE: the Fed HIKED to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16. The research phase's 06:03 macro block inferred a DOVISH FOMC from the 2026-09-17 tape — stocks and bonds rallying together — and built twenty minutes of work on that inference before checking the statement at 06:31 and finding it was a hike. A fully-priced hike produces the same tape signature. The correction is the accurate version and it is what every idea here now rests on; the FRED effective-fed-funds print of 3.63% quoted in the earlier block is the PRE-hike reading. Three ideas were rewritten as a direct result: TLT's short thesis was right by accident and is now correctly grounded (win probability raised 0.36 -> 0.42), EEM's stated driver was BACKWARDS — it was bought as a Fed-easing trade and a hiking Fed with a firmer dollar is a headwind, so it survives on its own price evidence alone and is held rather than added to (0.42 -> 0.34), and GLD's easing leg is dead with only the 3.4% core-PCE inflation leg surviving (0.40 -> 0.33). Read EEM and GLD knowing their original reason for existing did not survive verification.

COMPOSITION, STATED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED: 10 of these 12 are UPDATES TO OPEN POSITIONS, not new risk. Only MU and KMX are genuinely new ideas. With 16 live positions and a tape offering few clean new setups, managing the open book was the higher-value work; the skew is real and is reported rather than padded. There are no per-horizon quotas and nothing was dropped for variety — 9 swing, 2 long_term, 0 intraday is simply what cleared.

CONCENTRATION — THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT HERE. The five stated correlation buckets each sit at or under the 3-idea cap (rate-sensitive consumer: LCII, KMX and the watchlisted NKE; energy/refining: DINO, XLE; datacenter power: CEG, CCJ; pharma/biotech: PFE, SVRA; rates/macro: TLT short, EEM, GLD), but that tidiness is misleading and should not be trusted. The rate path is not one of five buckets — it is the factor underneath most of the book. TLT, EEM and GLD key off it directly, CEG is discounted by it, and all three consumer names sit at 120-day lows because of it. A single repricing of the long end moves ten of twelve lines together. Size the book, not the ideas.

RATIO CLUSTERING, DISCLOSED: six ideas land between 2.10 and 2.32 against a 2.0 swing floor (DINO 2.10, XLE 2.13, CEG 2.18, EEM 2.27, GLD 2.29, KMX 2.32), which is the signature of targets fitted to clear the bar. Here it is not, and the reason is checkable: five of the six are filled open positions whose entry, target and stop are all unchanged from their original publication, so the ratio is inherited rather than set today, and no stop was walked in on any of them. DINO in particular was NOT given a raised stop despite being +8.5% — at 116.62 a stop near 105 would sit 0.57 ATR from entry and fail the stop floor, which is the exact free-ratio manoeuvre the validator exists to refuse. The sixth, KMX, is new and is published as a WAIT with an explicit limit: at the 58.38 last close its ratio is 1.78 and FAILS the floor, so the bar is cleared by demanding a better price rather than by moving the target.

NKE IS DEMOTED TO THE WATCHLIST, and the reader should see why. Its target was LOWERED today from 62.00 to 53.11 because the old one sat above everything in the fetched 120-day history; that drops reward-to-risk from the filled 40.75 entry to 1.15 against a 2.5 long_term floor, so it cannot be published as a recommendation. It is not dropped silently, because the reader holds it at -10.8% and needs the decision: hold into the 2026-09-28 print, do not add. The ratio got worse as a direct result of an honest correction, and moving the target back up to fix it would be the failure, not the fix.

ALSO ON THE WATCHLIST, because the reader holds them: BCC, LULU and DVN are open positions that no longer clear on arithmetic, each worked through with fetched levels. Five unfilled orders are recommended for CANCELLATION rather than carried — VST @ 128.00, DG @ 134.50, IYR @ 103.60, BTC @ 63,400 and /MBTU6 @ 64,340; the two crypto shorts sit 18-19% below a spot of $78,143 on a contract at or past expiry. The book also holds offsetting pairs in NKE and LULU that should be reconciled rather than run side by side.

CHANGES MADE TO OPEN POSITIONS TODAY: LCII gained a 79.00 stop it never had while sitting 37.4% off its high; TLT gained both a target (78.00) and a stop (83.30), having been carried since 2026-09-02 with neither. Those are the two real defects fixed. No stop was tightened anywhere.

COVERAGE GAPS AND FAILED SOURCES. No intraday idea was published for a concrete reason: the nasdaq `history` source returned computed aggregates but a NULL per-bar OHLC array for every symbol, so no intraday or swing support/resistance could be read at all. Every level in this report is set off SMA20/SMA50, the 120-day range and ATR14 — which is also why several rejects failed for 'no target that clears', since the only levels available to aim at were the range extremes. SMA200 is null on every name (120 bars fetched), so no long-term trend filter was applied. Event contracts were unreachable: `market_data.py events` matched only KXMVECROSSCATEGORY sports parlays on every macro query tried (Fed, FEDDECISION, CPI, inflation, recession, rate, gold, bitcoin), so the three KXFEDDECISION rows in prior context could not be re-priced and no event idea was invented. Crypto spot was fetched but `history` has no crypto source, so ATR and stop distances were impossible and no crypto candidate is publishable. Options-implied moves are unavailable (yahoo-options HTTP 401), which matters most for MU, whose 30.7% target could NOT be checked against what the straddle prices. Short interest timed out against api.nasdaq.com. Yahoo returned HTTP 429 throughout, so ^VIX, DXY, WTI and all index and futures quotes failed and ETF proxies were used instead. Working: FRED, finnhub, CoinGecko, api.nasdaq.com history/insiders/analysts/relstrength, SEC EDGAR, federalreserve.gov.

PRICES: all equity and ETF prices are the 2026-09-17 16:00 ET close, re-quoted during the 06:0x ET pre-session and unchanged from research. That is a closed market, not stale data — it is the freshest honest print at this hour.

TRACK RECORD CONTEXT: 7 closed trades of 32 tracked, 1 hit target. That is far under the ~15 needed to mean anything, so it is noise and has not been over-fitted to. Conviction 2 is 0/2 — the three conviction-2 ideas here (CCJ, SVRA, GLD) are all existing 1% positions held rather than added to, and CCJ is explicitly flagged as a third appearance in ten days that has gone backwards throughout.

RED TEAM (phase 2c). Cut 4 of 12, downgraded 3, trimmed 2 on size, and reversed 3 mechanical flags as validator artifacts. Eight recommendations survive.

THE PATTERN WORTH THE MOST: four ideas carried headline reward-to-risk ratios that were artifacts of unreachable targets — the mirror image of the walked-in stop this repo already guards against, and it clears the floor just as freely. A ratio improves as easily by aiming somewhere price cannot get as by moving the stop closer, and neither is work. LCII (2.93), CCJ (3.57) and SVRA (3.53) all had targets 11.8-13.2 ATR away inside a 15-session swing horizon; two of the three sat at or above the 120-day high. Re-anchored to reachable levels none of them pays: LCII gives 0.56:1 at its SMA50 and needs +43.4% from spot to clear 2.0, CCJ needs +26.1% with no dated catalyst from the weakest name in its group, and SVRA has NO target at or below its 120-day high that clears the floor at all. All three are cut to the watchlist with the arithmetic shown. GLD is the fourth cut and the only one killed on thesis rather than geometry: the one leg surviving the Fed hike is 3.4% core PCE, and the same SEP the idea cites projects it to 2.5% by 2027, so the mechanism is falsified by its own source; 2.6pp of claimed edge over a 30.4% break-even is inside the noise.

Three of these four were killed by sentences the synthesis phase had already written and then not acted on — CCJ's 'a broken position being held out of anchoring', SVRA's 'opening it fresh today on this evidence would not be' defensible, GLD's 'a reasonable reader could close this rather than hold it'. That is the generate-and-critique-at-once problem the separate phase exists for, and the write-ups were honest enough to make the job easy.

DOWNGRADES. PFE 4 -> 3: the claim carrying 17.8pp of edge — that the estimates are wrong and not the business — is the one the author states is asserted rather than demonstrated, no revenue trajectory having been fetched. MU 4 -> 3: a binary earnings trade whose own key_risk concedes the 872 stop cannot enforce the stated risk, into a 91.4%-bullish book; a 4 gets sized largest and this is the idea least able to hold its stop. EEM 3 -> 2 and trimmed 2% -> 1%: its driver was falsified by the research phase itself, and both remaining confirmations are read off one fetched price series, so it is nearer one confirmation than two against a 3.4pp edge.

STOP-WIDENING TEST, run on all eight survivors and reported whether or not it flatters them. Widened to the ATR level where this report's stop-outs have clustered, TLT holds at 2.45 (from 2.71), MU at 2.75, KMX at 2.22, XLE at 2.21 and EEM at 2.62 — those ratios are real. CEG falls to 1.78 and DINO to 1.88, both under the 2.0 floor; neither stop was walked in and both clear the floor as published, so they are kept with the failing test recorded on the idea rather than cut for it, and CEG is ranked last of the conviction-3s.

CORRELATION. XLE trimmed 3% -> 2%: XLE at 3% plus DINO at 2% was 5% of capital on one variable, and DINO is a constituent of XLE, so XLE's sector-internals evidence is literally the other position. DINO is separately instructed to take partial profit — its inherited 2.10 ratio describes a trade already more than half done, and the forward reward from 116.62 is 11.38 against 18.87 to the stop, or 0.60:1. Neither stop is tightened to improve that; trimming size is the honest way down. The report's broader caveat stands and is not fixable by cutting: the long end is still the factor under most of the book.

THREE VALIDATION FAILURES REVERSED, each verified against a live fetch rather than waved away.
(1) `sources` FAILED all 12 ideas on one URL — https://api.nasdaq.com/api/quote/<SYM>/historical. That is not a hallucinated citation: it is the exact endpoint scripts/market_data.py:493 calls for price history, minus the assetclass/fromdate/todate query string it requires, so a bare HEAD returns 404. Left in place, phase 2d --enforce would have demoted every surviving recommendation to the watchlist on a data-fetch path. It is removed from the `sources` array on all eight survivors, which each retain their remaining citations, and DELIBERATELY LEFT IN `evidence[].source` where it records real provenance. This is a gap in check_sources, not in the report — an API path should not be judged by the same rule as a published page. A test and a fix belong in scripts/validate_report.py; that is a code change, not a red-team edit, so it is flagged here rather than made this morning.
(2) `earnings_date` flagged MU and KMX as absent from the calendar and FAILED LCII outright. Re-fetched at 06:37 ET: MU 2026-09-30 amc, KMX 2026-09-29 and THO 2026-09-22 bmo are all confirmed, and the cause of the flag is now pinned rather than guessed. validate_report.py calls md.earnings(45); that response truncates at exactly 1500 rows and the cut falls across the near dates, so the 45-day window returns 1500 symbols containing NONE of MU, KMX or THO, while the 14-, 21- and 30-day windows return all three consistently. A longer lookahead silently returning FEWER near-dated symbols than a shorter one is the bug, and it will mis-flag every dated catalyst in every future report until the fetch is paged or the window shortened. LCII's 'failure' was the validator comparing LCII's own 2026-10-28 print against a catalyst that is explicitly THO's — the date was right and the check read the wrong symbol. (LCII is still cut, on its target, not on this.)
(3) `spread` FAILED KMX (8.64%), LCII (48.43%), DINO (10.68%) and SVRA (27.98%) at 06:34 ET. Every one of those asks sits above the symbol's own 2026-09-17 regular-session high — LCII's 138.38 ask against an 89.22 high, DINO's 127.98 against 116.69, KMX's 64.13 against 59.98, SVRA's 6.07 against 5.47. These are closed-market book artifacts, not tradeable spreads: check_price_freshness distinguishes a closed market from stale data and check_spread does not. The residue that IS real is liquidity — LCII at $22.3M and SVRA at $7.8M of daily dollar volume are thin, and every entry here is a limit order, never a market one.

NOT CUT, AND SAID PLAINLY. TLT was attacked hardest as the highest-conviction idea left and kept at 4: it is the only recommendation resting on a primary document read directly, its target is derived from duration arithmetic rather than drawn, and it survives the stop-widening test. KMX kept at 4 because it refuses the current price rather than moving its target — a WAIT with a stated limit is the right way to clear a floor. No target was moved further out anywhere in this pass, and no stop was tightened.

WHAT PHASE 2d WILL STILL DEMOTE, FLAGGED IN ADVANCE RATHER THAN WORKED AROUND. After the `sources` artifact was removed, six of the eight survivors pass or warn. KMX (8.64%) and DINO (9.82%) still FAIL `spread`, on the same closed-market book documented above — both quoted asks sit above the symbol's own 2026-09-17 regular-session high, so neither is a spread anyone could trade against. --enforce will send both to the watchlist anyway, and that is left to run: the fetched number is not mine to overrule, and quietly editing around an enforcement gate is the exact behaviour phases 2b-2d exist to prevent. It is recorded here, and on each idea, so the demotion is contestable on the record rather than mistaken for a finding about the trade. KMX in particular is a LIMIT order at 56.00 with an explicit do-not-pay-up condition — it never crosses a spread at the market — and check_spread has no way to know that. Re-running validation after the open, when a real book exists, is what would settle it. Validation demoted 2 idea(s) whose numbers did not check out. 6 more carry warnings — see the validation block on each.

catalyst.event: The FOMC raised the target range 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 with core PCE projected at 3.4% for 2026, and the September dot plot puts the median fed funds rate at 4.1% by end-2026 — one further hike from the current 3.875% midpoint, then held at 4.1% through 2027
catalyst.action: UPDATE to an open short. Hold. A target at 78.00 and a stop at 83.30 are ADDED — this position has been carried since 2026-09-02 with neither, which is the defect being fixed today. This is a short and requires margin.

recommendations.thesis: Open short from 2026-09-02 at 81.87, now 81.78. This is the position best supported by what the Fed actually did on 2026-09-16: it hiked to 3.75-4.00%, projects core PCE at 3.4% for 2026, and its own median dot implies another hike to 4.1% before year-end with no cut until 2028. Chair Warsh said inflation is too high and has been for too long. A central bank still tightening against 3.4% core inflation is the plainest case there is for long-duration Treasuries continuing lower, and a 20-year-plus ETF is the purest short expression available on this venue.
recommendations.key_risk: Short duration is the crowded side of this trade and the squeeze risk is real — TLT rallied 1.11% on 2026-09-17, the day after the hike, against the position. The 83.30 stop is only 1.75% above the entry, so a single risk-off session closes it. If inflation rolls over faster than the SEP assumes, or if growth cracks and the market prices cuts through 2027 against the dots, long bonds rally hard. Being short requires margin and the position can gap beyond the stop.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that most of the move has already happened: TLT is only 1.64% above its 120-day low of 80.46, so the obvious chart target is roughly where price already sits, and reaching 78.00 requires breaking to new lows rather than continuing to one. That is why the target is derived from yield rather than drawn on the chart. The sharper version is that the hike is already in the price — the market knew it was coming and bonds *rose* the next session anyway, which is exactly the behaviour of an asset that has finished discounting the news. If the long end does not extend past roughly 5.3%, this position does not pay from here even if the direction is right. RED TEAM: attacked hardest as the highest-conviction idea left, and kept at 4. It is the only recommendation resting on a primary document read directly rather than a story about it, its target is derived from duration arithmetic and stated as the yield claim it is, and it passes the test the ratio usually fails: widened from 2.04 to the 2.25 ATR ETF cluster level (stop 83.45), the reward-to-risk is still 2.45 and clears the floor, so the 2.71 is not a stop-distance artifact. The unanswered objection stays the one above — bonds rose the session after the hike, and if the long end stalls short of ~5.3% this does not pay even if the direction is right.

evidence.detail: Fetched 120-day history: close 81.78, ATR14 0.7015 (0.86%), SMA20 82.01, SMA50 82.68, range 80.46-87.79. Price is below both moving averages, confirming the downtrend. The added 83.30 stop is 1.43 above the filled short entry = 2.04 ATR, clearing the 1.8 ATR ETF swing floor, and sits above both the SMA20 and SMA50, so it is placed beyond real resistance rather than inside it.

Read the FOMC implementation note and the Summary of Economic Projections directly rather than a story about them. Target range raised 25bp to 3-3/4 to 4 percent effective 2026-09-17; IORB 3.90%, primary credit 4.00%, standing repo 4.00%, ON RRP 3.75%. SEP medians: fed funds 4.1% end-2026, 4.1% end-2027, 3.9% end-2028, 3.2% longer run; PCE inflation 3.7% and core PCE 3.4% for 2026; unemployment 4.1%; GDP 2.3%.

The 78.00 target is derived, not drawn. TLT effective duration is approximately 17 years, so a further ~30bp rise in long-end yields from the fetched 5.01% 10-year to roughly 5.3% implies about -5% on the fund: 81.87 -> ~77.8. Target set at 78.00 on that arithmetic and stated as the yield claim it actually is.

catalyst.event: Post-COVID normalisation completing while the market still prices a melting ice cube — the driver is the re-rating of a business that keeps beating, not a dated event
catalyst.action: UPDATE to an open position and a continuing accumulation, not a new idea. Add in the 26.50-28.10 zone; add again only below 25.00. No stop by design — the invalidation is a business condition, stated in key_risk, not a price.

recommendations.thesis: Open position from 2026-08-18 at 27.60, now 27.64 — flat, and the thesis is a multi-year re-rating rather than a move. The mispricing is visible in two fetched numbers that disagree with each other: only 38.9% of covering analysts are bullish and that share is still falling, while the company has beaten consensus in each of the last three reported quarters by 11.37%, 3.55% and 14.29%. A business that consistently beats while its analyst base gets more negative is one where the published estimates, not the business, are what is wrong. Downside case is 23.50, or about 8.1x, which is where this is worth owning even if the pipeline disappoints.
recommendations.key_risk: The concrete invalidation, since there is deliberately no stop: two consecutive quarters of EPS misses against consensus, or guidance that puts post-LOE revenue replacement materially behind schedule, would mean the beats were cost-driven rather than a real earnings base and the 14.5x multiple is not owed. A patent-cliff business can beat quarterly numbers for years while its terminal earnings power still erodes, and that is the specific way this thesis is wrong.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that 38.9% bullish and deteriorating is not necessarily a contrarian signal — it may simply be correct, and the consistent beats may be cost cuts and buybacks against a shrinking revenue base rather than evidence of an earnings floor. I cannot fully answer that from what was fetched today: I have three quarters of EPS actuals but no revenue trajectory, so the quality of the beats is asserted rather than demonstrated. The multiple, not the growth, has to carry the idea. The win probability is set at 0.40 rather than higher for exactly this reason: against a 22.2% baseline that is still ~18pp of claimed edge, which is as much as an unverified earnings-quality argument can carry. RED TEAM: conviction lowered 4 -> 3 on this paragraph rather than despite it. The thesis is that the estimates are wrong and not the business, and the author states the quality of the beats is asserted rather than demonstrated — no revenue trajectory was fetched, so the one claim carrying 17.8pp of edge over a 22.2% break-even is the one that could not be checked. The three evidence kinds are real; the valuation anchor among them annualises 2.18 of EPS from three quarters into ~2.90, which is a construction, not a fetched TTM figure. That is a 3.

evidence.detail: Method shown, inputs are fetched actuals rather than a remembered figure: reported EPS of 0.77 (Q2 26), 0.75 (Q1 26) and 0.66 (Q4 25) sum to 2.18 over three quarters, annualising to roughly 2.90. The 23.50 bear case is ~8.1x and independently coincides with the fetched 120-day low of 23.62. NOTE: 2.90 is annualised from three fetched quarters, not a fetched trailing-twelve-month figure. Long-term R:R against the bear case = 14.40/4.10 = 3.51.
